title: File-based GNSS signal chain: gps-sdr-sim => GNSS-SDR => spoofing/jamming scorer
summary: A Docker (arm64/amd64) testbed that never transmits: gps-sdr-sim synthesizes GPS L1 C/A IQ for a static receiver from the shipped 2022-01-01 broadcast ephemeris, a numpy mixer adds noise, a second spoofer stream (power offset, time offset, ramp) and/or a jamming burst, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 processes each file into PVT, RINEX and a PVT dump, and an adapter feeds the 1 Hz epochs (position, clock, per-SV C/N0) into the gnss-interference-monitor scorer. Four scenarios: clean, unaligned overpower, jam-then-spoof, and a code/carrier-aligned drag-off that walks the fix 978 m away.
verified: ran end to end on 2026-11-06 with Docker arm64 on Apple Silicon (./run.sh, 223 s): gps-sdr-sim commit 28ca29a, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 package), RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 rnx2rtkp. Real outputs are in out/ and quoted in the README: clean median horizontal error 3.0 m with 0 scorer alerts; drag-off captured the PVT to 977.8 m off truth with the first scorer alert at t=67 s and a missed stretch t=87-129 s; unaligned overpower and jam-then-spoof caused a GNSS-SDR PVT outage, not a capture. GNSS-SDR runs are not bit-identical between runs. Not validated against a hardware receiver; the AGC input is a file-power proxy.
